Joe Rogan argues that modern comforts are making us weak in a segment from his show. The claim is a pet theme of his: soft beds, soft food, and soft days breed soft men. Rogan hosts the rant in his own voice.

Rogan works through the case, from chairs and screens to drugs that numb each ache. He urges cold, strain, and hard tasks as the cure his own life taught him. The segment is short and built to fire up his crowd. Listeners get a brisk dose of Rogan grit. The library holds the file as an archive record of the take.

An expert in intelligent design discusses the Big Bang and the James Webb Space Telescope in this Joe Rogan Experience segment. The Webb telescope has sent back images of very early galaxies that surprised many astronomers. Design advocates see those surprises as cracks in the standard story of the cosmos.

The guest argues that the early, orderly galaxies Webb found fit a designed universe better than a chance one. Rogan asks how the claim handles the strong evidence for cosmic expansion and great age. They also cover what design says about life's origin. The segment gives the design case a friendly hearing on a huge platform.
